text: In Genesis 22 the three days of travel are a kind of suspended sentence; outwardly nothing happens, and yet in significance everything happens. The servants, the wood, the knife, and the fire are named with care, so that the instruments of the act stand ready before the act itself. Obedience and horror remain side by side, and neither is suffered to prevail. Faith here is no affair of feeling; it takes the form of a structured relation, an arrangement between God, Abraham, and Isaac.
